answer: Before filing, the filer must light the town beacon for one night watch: the crystal lens throws its beam across the valley and the plume rises in plain sight of every neighbour. The desk checks the town log within a day — the light burned all night, the plume was seen from two towns, and the next watcher signed. No watch, a dark lamp, or a forged signature means rejection and a 250-coin bond forfeit, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 real night watches plus 250,000 coins. One operator filed forty claims on forty forged logs, and all forty fell when no neighbour had seen any beam.
